The names of competitions, teams and players are used only descriptively, for historical purposes. The app uses no logos, emblems, official trophies or photographs.

Lucien Laurent scored the first goal in World Cup history, in minute 19.
The first ever final. The teams could not agree on a ball, so Argentina's was used in the first half and Uruguay's in the second.
The first final decided in extra time: Angelo Schiavio scored the winner in minute 95.
Ernst Wilimowski scored 4 for Poland and still lost — Leônidas replied with 3.
Italy became the first team to retain the title. Vittorio Pozzo is still the only coach to win two World Cups.
One of the biggest upsets ever: the part-timers of the USA beat England at England's first World Cup.
The "Maracanazo": in front of almost 200,000 fans at the Maracanã, Uruguay won the title. Brazil only needed a draw.
West Germany fielded a side full of reserves. Puskás injured his ankle in this match.
The "Miracle of Bern": Hungary had been unbeaten for almost four years and led 2–0 after 8 minutes.
The highest-scoring match in World Cup history: 12 goals, played in scorching heat in Lausanne.
Just Fontaine scored 4 and reached 13 goals at a single World Cup — a record that still stands.
Pelé, only 17, scored twice in the final. Brazil's first world title.
Remembered as the "Battle of Santiago", one of the most violent matches ever played.
Pak Doo-ik's goal knocked Italy out — one of the tournament's greatest upsets.
North Korea led 3–0 after 25 minutes. Eusébio scored 4 and turned the match around.
Antonio Rattín's sending-off inspired referee Ken Aston to invent yellow and red cards, used from 1970.
Geoff Hurst scored the first hat-trick in a final. His third goal, off the crossbar, is still debated today.
The "Game of the Century": 5 goals in extra time, with Beckenbauer playing on with a dislocated shoulder in a sling.
Brazil's third title, which let them keep the Jules Rimet trophy for good. Carlos Alberto's goal is hailed as one of the finest team goals ever.
The only official match between the two German states. Jürgen Sparwasser scored the winner for East Germany.
The Dutch scored a penalty in minute 2, before any German had touched the ball — and still lost the final.
Argentina needed to win by at least four goals to reach the final.
Argentina's first title. In the 90th minute, Rob Rensenbrink hit the post for the Netherlands.
Algeria beat West Germany but went out after the "Disgrace of Gijón". Since then, final group games kick off at the same time.
The only World Cup match in which a team scored 10 goals.
Paolo Rossi scored three times to knock out the Brazil of Zico and Sócrates. He ended the tournament as champion and top scorer.
The first penalty shoot-out in World Cup history. France had led 3–1 in extra time.
Within four minutes, Maradona scored the "Hand of God" and then the "Goal of the Century", after a run from his own half.
West Germany came back from 0–2, but Burruchaga scored the winner in minute 84 from a Maradona pass.
In the opening match, Cameroon beat the reigning champions while finishing with only nine men.
The first final with a player sent off: Pedro Monzón. Andreas Brehme won it with a penalty in minute 85.
Hagi's goal in minute 34 was a lob from around 40 metres, out near the touchline. Colombia were seen as one of the favourites.
One of Romania's greatest matches: Dumitrescu scored twice and Romania reached the quarter-finals for the first time.
Răducioiu put Romania ahead in extra time, but Sweden equalised in minute 115. In the shoot-out, Ravelli saved from Petrescu and Belodedici.
Oleg Salenko scored 5 goals — the record for a single match. Roger Milla, aged 42, became the oldest scorer.
The first final decided on penalties. Roberto Baggio sent the last kick over the bar.
Before this match, Romania's players dyed their hair blond, keeping a promise made once they qualified from the group.
Lilian Thuram scored both goals — his only goals in 142 matches for France.
Zidane scored two headers and France won their first world title, on home soil.
At their first World Cup, Senegal beat the reigning champions in the opening match.
Ahn Jung-hwan sent South Korea through with a "golden goal" in extra time.
Ronaldo scored twice to reach 8 goals at the tournament. Brazil's fifth title — a record.
In the last match of his career, Zidane was sent off for headbutting Materazzi.
In the last minute of extra time, Suárez stopped a certain goal with his hand. Gyan missed the penalty and Uruguay won the shoot-out.
Iniesta scored in minute 116 to give Spain their first world title.
A rematch of the 2010 final, featuring Robin van Persie's flying header from the edge of the box.
Germany scored 5 goals in the first 29 minutes. Klose reached 16 goals — the all-time record.
Substitute Mario Götze scored in minute 113. The first title won by a European team in the Americas.
The reigning champions went out in the group stage — a first for Germany since 1938.
The first own goal in a final (Mandžukić) and the first penalty awarded in a final with the help of VAR.
The only defeat of the eventual champions at this tournament.
Morocco became the first African team to reach a World Cup semi-final.
Mbappé scored the second hat-trick in a final, after Hurst in 1966. Messi scored twice and finally won the World Cup.
